title: Dairy Processing Unit Operations — Separation, Standardisation, Pasteurisation, Sterilisation, Homogenisation, Concentration
shortDescription: The core dairy-plant operations with the principles and numbers examiners use.
genZNote: Receive, clean, split, set, heat, break up, concentrate — dairy plant's daily routine. LTLT vs HTST vs UHT numbers = easy marks.

sections.heading: Flow and Operations
sections.body: Pearson square example: to standardise 100 kg milk of 4.5% fat to 3.0% using skim milk of 0.05% fat, mix in the ratio (4.5 − 3.0) : (3.0 − 0.05) of skim : milk = 1.5 : 2.95.

table.caption: Unit operations
rows: Temperature, sensory, COB (clot on boiling), alcohol test, acidity, fat/SNF, adulterants
Centrifugal force; disc-bowl separator; Stokes' law; skim and cream
Adjust fat/SNF to a standard; Pearson square method
LTLT 63 °C/30 min; HTST 72 °C/15 s; check by alkaline phosphatase test (negative)
UHT 135–150 °C for a few seconds with aseptic packing; in-bottle sterilisation 110–120 °C for 10–20 min
Force through valve at ~150–250 bar (two-stage possible); reduces fat globules <1–2 µm, prevents creaming
Evaporation under vacuum at lower temperature (multiple-effect/falling-film evaporators); membrane processes also used

sections.heading: Why Each Step Exists
bullets: Pasteurisation kills vegetative pathogens (e.g. Coxiella burnetii, Mycobacterium) without major quality loss; phosphatase test confirms; peroxidase test shows overheating.
UHT milk is commercially sterile and can be stored at ambient temperature for months in aseptic packs.
Homogenisation improves stability, mouthfeel and whiteness but increases susceptibility to light-induced oxidation.
Concentration reduces transport and drying cost and increases shelf life.

sections.heading: Exam Notes
bullets: Order of conditions: LTLT lowest temperature, longest time; UHT highest, shortest.
Separation: lighter fat moves inward; skim leaves at the periphery.
Cleaning-in-place cycles protect plant hygiene (see Dairy Quality lesson).

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Dairy unit operations convert raw milk into safe, stable, standardised ingredients using separation, heat treatment, homogenisation and concentration.

commonTraps: Do not say pasteurised milk is sterile.
